summary.headline: Yatharth Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 3,927 mn with record EBITDA of INR 917 mn; consolidated EBITDA margin 23.3%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR 3,927 mn (up 51% YoY, 15% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 917 mn, with PAT of INR 454 mn. Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra) contributed 27% of revenue. Faridabad Sector 20 reached EBITDA breakeven in about 9 months, while the group margin was diluted by new-hospital losses (adjusted margin ex-New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 was 28.1%). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of upwards of 24% EBITDA margin and ARPOB growth of 8-10%, and announced a maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value.

segments.name: Existing hospitals (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Jhansi-Orchha)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 2,862 mn, +22% YoY; Noida and Jhansi-Orchha at 90%+ occupancy, Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56%. ARPOB: Noida Extension above INR 50,000, Greater Noida ~INR 43,000, Noida ~INR 35,000, Jhansi ~INR 13,000.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 1,067 mn (27% of revenue). Faridabad Sector 20 at monthly revenue INR 12-13 crore, ARPOB near INR 40,000, EBITDA breakeven in ~9 months. Model Town at INR 8 crore monthly run rate, ARPOB near INR 50,000, breakeven guided to Q3-Q4 FY27. Agra at INR 9-10 crore run rate with 20%+ EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Contributing close to 10% of group revenue with one LINAC at Noida Extension; additional LINACs being added at Faridabad Sector 20 and then New Delhi.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management says it is on track for guidance on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with upside possible on some parameters; EBITDA margin upwards of 24% (guided 24-25%).
ARPOB growth of 8-10% YoY for FY27 and each year thereafter.

Bed capacity: announced capacity above 3,200 beds (incl. 250-bed Gurugram live in Q1 FY28 and ~450 brownfield beds in Noida cluster over ~15-19 months); target of 5,000 beds now expected in about 2.5 years.
New hospitals expected to reach 25%+ EBITDA margin (~27%) within two years; Faridabad Sector 20 and Model Town to reach 15-20% EBITDA margin about 15-18 months after breakeven.
Depreciation guided at ~INR 29 crore per quarter for the next three quarters; no fresh loans planned in FY27.
Dividend: maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value approved.
capex_capacity: Census beds 1,820 vs 1,655 last quarter; 2,555 total beds in existing network per management.
Gurugram 250-bed hospital under construction, expected to go live in Q1 FY28 with ARPOB potential of INR 50,000+; cost ~INR 1 crore per bed.
Brownfield expansion at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (~450 beds): construction delayed by monsoon; capacity coming live in 15-18 months.
Capex per bed guided at INR 75-80 lakh for the remaining ~1,800 beds (greenfield, brownfield, acquisitions, lease models), up from INR 61.4 lakh cited by an analyst over three years.
Agra: 250 beds installed but only 110 census beds operational; plan to increase census beds.
Funding: acquisition partly debt-funded (~INR 80 crore); management says it is comfortable up to ~2x TTM group EBITDA in debt and will use internal accruals going forward.
demand_pricing: Group ARPOB INR 34,758 (+7% YoY); new NCR premium hospitals (Noida Extension, New Delhi) crossed INR 50,000 for the first time in Q1.

Payer mix: government share ~40% at group level (analyst noted 36% last quarter); attributed to ~2% impact from recent CGHS rate revision, with government volumes declining QoQ. Newer hospitals have under 10% government business and 90%+ cash and private insurance.
Average length of stay fell below 4 days for the first time, attributed to lower government mix and surgical mix in new hospitals.
Doctor attrition ~7% group-wide; senior doctor attrition below 3-4%.
Incremental EBITDA margin on additional occupancy (e.g. Faridabad Sector 20 to 70%) estimated at 22-23%.
Regulatory: a panel recommended capping hospital room rents at 3-star hotel levels; management declined to comment in detail and said no framework has been received yet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5,000-bed target three years or five, and will new beds be in existing clusters or new ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 5,000-bed target could be reached in about 2.5 years, earlier than the three-year target, mainly in North India (NCR, Gurugram), with new clusters such as UP and state capitals under evaluation. Announced capacity is already above 3,200 beds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy at Greater Faridabad and Model Town stagnate, and what are the government and insurance mix trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lower occupancy to census bed increases (Model Town census beds 100 to 150; new Faridabad 100 to 200), not weak demand. Government mix at newer hospitals is under 10%, and empanelments are largely complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of the 3,200 beds and current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurugram's 250 beds go live in Q1 FY28; around 450 Noida-cluster brownfield beds come live in about 15-19 months (200 earlier, 250 at 18-19 months). Nitin Gupta cited 2,800 capacity including Gurugram.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be met and what is the ARPOB growth expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for FY27 revenue, EBITDA and PAT guidance, with some parameters possibly surpassed. EBITDA margin is guided upwards of 24%, and ARPOB growth at 9-10% (8-10% as stated later).

qa_highlights.question: How is quarterly revenue derived from ARPOB, occupancy and census beds?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Gupta said ARPOB of about INR 35,000 on 1,820 census beds at 68% occupancy reconciles to revenue, with ARPOB including IPD and OPD. Hospital-level occupancy given: Noida 91%, Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56%, Greater Faridabad 63%, new Faridabad 49%, Model Town 29%, Agra 89%, Jhansi 91%.

qa_highlights.question: When will the newer assets reach a margin in line with the group, and when will the group return to 26-27% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Faridabad Sector 20 is breakeven with a 4-5% margin drag; Model Town is guided to breakeven in Q3-Q4 FY27. Both should reach 15-20% margin about 15-18 months after breakeven. Management said group margin would stay near 24%, not 28%, given ongoing new additions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a view on the CGHS room rent cap proposal, and what is the government payer mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Kumar Singh said there is no comment yet, as no framework has been received. Yatharth Tyagi noted past government support for private hospitals and recent CGHS rate revisions. Group government mix is about 40%, with the increase attributed to a 1-2% CGHS price revision rather than volume.

risks_watch: Margin dilution from new hospitals: group adjusted margin 28.1% vs reported 23.3%; Model Town breakeven slipped risk (guided Q3-Q4 FY27) and Gurugram drag from FY28.
Occupancy ramp at Noida Extension (56%), Model Town (29%) and new Faridabad (49%); census bed additions are distorting occupancy comparisons.
Interest cost rose to INR 6.6 crore from INR 5 crore QoQ; debt ~INR 300 crore vs ~INR 210 crore in March; PAT margin under pressure; management targets ~2x TTM EBITDA as debt ceiling.
Regulatory risk: panel proposal to cap hospital room rents at 3-star hotel levels; no framework yet and management declined detailed comment.
Brownfield expansions at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (~450 beds) delayed by monsoon; 15-19 month timeline; Agra only 110 of 250 beds operational.
Capex per bed rising to INR 75-80 lakh for remaining ~1,800 beds; doctor attrition ~7% group-wide and cost increase of ~2% QoQ in doctor fees within other expenses.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to report a strong start of F Y27. We delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and profits this quarter.
As far as Delhi is concerned, we are sticking to our guidance. We expect that hospital to break even around 15 to 17 months.
I think the pressure should decrease from here going forward because this much high capex is not being planned any time for any of the coming quarters soon.
As of now, we don't want to comment on it. As industry moves on, when we receive some frameworks, then probably it will be appropriate for us to comment and see that.
So, I think the company is on track to meet that guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, breakeven timelines and FY27 guidance, with management stating it is on track and some parameters may be exceeded. Cautious and non-committal on the CGHS room-rent cap proposal and on any group margin return to 28%.
